messages:
oliver: Heads up — running into a weird hang in a Jupyter notebook when calling the async client from a top-level cell. The cell never finishes and kernel CPU spikes.

oliver: Minimal example below (IPython 8.15, python 3.11):
```python
from redwood import AsyncClient

client = AsyncClient(api_key='REDACTED')
# in notebook cell (not inside async def)
resp = client.generate('hello')
print(resp)
```

oliver: Instead of error it just blocks. If I do `await client.generate('hello')` in a cell with `ipython` builtin async support it works fine.

priya: Jupyter has a running loop already (IPython integrates with asyncio). If your code returns a coroutine and you never await it, the cell will show a coroutine object but shouldn't hang — odd. Any chance the sync wrapper is calling `asyncio.get_event_loop().run_until_complete`?

luke: We actually have a convenience `.sync()` helper on the sync Client but not on AsyncClient. Might be that people try to call async methods without awaiting them and some helper auto-drives the loop badly.

oliver: Checked the stack with `CTRL-C` during the hang — stack shows httpx._client running and waiting on socket read. But I also see `nest_asyncio` being imported in another extension.

priya: nest_asyncio can patch the loop to allow nested runs, but it can also cause weird interactions with libraries that expect a clean loop. Does the kernel log show "Event loop is closed" or similar?

oliver: No closed-loop error. Just stuck in httpx read. If I explicitly `await client.generate` it returns instantly.

luke: Could be that whoever created `client = AsyncClient()` outside an async context created an AsyncClient whose transport is not fully initialized until entering the async context. Using the client without async context may open connections lazily and the background tasks get scheduled weirdly.

priya: Workaround for notebooks: either use the sync Client or use `await client.aclose()` in a cell before re-instantiating. Also `async with AsyncClient(...) as c:` inside an `await` cell works.

oliver: Agreed. For UX we should improve docs and maybe add a convenience `AsyncClient.start_sync()` that ensures proper initialization when used from sync contexts (not ideal but helpful in notebooks).

luke: Filing issue #412 to track: add notebook guide + a `run_sync_compat` helper and better error message when AsyncClient methods are called from sync contexts and return coroutine objects.

docs-bot: Issue created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/412 (title: "AsyncClient: notebook deadlocks and sync-compat helpers")

oliver: Also running into typing annoyance: my editor suggests `generate()` returns Any. Can we publish more precise typing for `AsyncClient.generate -> Awaitable[GenerateResponse]`? Helps DX in notebooks.

priya: Good call — adding typing follow-up to #412. Also consider making the sync Client a thin wrapper around AsyncClient with `anyio.from_thread.run` so users in notebooks can call sync code without worrying about loop state.

luke: I pushed draft PR #820 that adds a short notebook doc, a helper `utils.ensure_async_client_started()` and two tests that run against IPython to simulate the running loop. CI kicking off.

ci-bot: PR #820 checks started — https://ci.example.com/redwood/sdk/820 :hourglass_flowing_sand:

oliver: Thanks. If PR includes a clear notebook example I'll link it in our internal onboarding. The current quickstart only shows sync server and plain async scripts, not notebooks.

priya: Action items: 1) update docs quickstart with Jupyter section, 2) add SyncClient wrapper example using anyio, 3) improve typing for AsyncClient methods, 4) add helpful runtime error when a coroutine is returned from public API without being awaited.

luke: Sounds good. Marking as assigned: luke -> implement helpers/tests, priya -> docs, oliver -> verify notebook examples on mac/linux.

oliver: Verified PR branch locally — notebook example fixed my hanging cell. Will re-run on another kernel and report back.

priya: Nice. Closing this thread for now, keep comments on #412. :rocket:
